questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Identify when an icon needs a text label to be understood
questions.stem: Maya's log shows a crescent icon beside a magnitude value; she wonders if readers will know it means 'waxing phase' without a label.

options.text: A short text label should accompany the icon so the magnitude entry stays unambiguous.

options.text: Labels are unnecessary once the icon appears more than twice in the same log.
The icon should be removed entirely and replaced with the numeric magnitude only.
options.misconception: ignores the phase information the icon carries

questions.explanation: Icons gain meaning from context, and a label removes ambiguity for new readers. Repetition alone does not teach an unfamiliar symbol.
questions.hint: Ask whether a first-time reader would decode the icon alone.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Read a magnitude axis correctly when smaller numbers mean brighter stars
questions.stem: In Raj's log, the y-axis lists magnitudes 2, 4, 6 from top to bottom; explain why a falling plotted point means the star is brightening.

answer.exemplar: A falling point moves toward smaller magnitude numbers, and smaller magnitudes mean brighter stars, so the star is brightening rather than dimming.

questions.explanation: Magnitude runs inverse to brightness, so descending the axis means brightening. Treating larger numbers as brighter reverses the true trend.
questions.hint: Remember that lower magnitude equals brighter in astronomy.

options.text: A bar chart is always better because pictures are easier to scan than numbers.

options.text: Either format works because focal length and price are unrelated quantities.

options.text: A table is better because readers need precise focal lengths and prices side by side.
A pie chart suits this data since each eyepiece is a slice of total cost.
options.misconception: misapplies part-to-whole chart to independent items

questions.explanation: When exact paired values drive the decision, a table keeps numbers precise. Charts excel at trends, not at reading exact paired figures.
questions.hint: Match the format to the reader's main task.
